name: Saint Cyril of Jerusalem
history: Bishop of Jerusalem in the stormy years after the Council of Nicaea, three times driven into exile. His Catechetical Lectures, given to those preparing for baptism at Easter, are a priceless picture of how the early Church taught the Creed and the sacraments. Leo XIII named him a Doctor of the Church in 1883.
life: Cyril was probably born in or near Jerusalem and was ordained priest there. Around 350 he gave his famous lectures in the Church of the Holy Sepulchre, built by Constantine over the place of the crucifixion and resurrection: a series on the Creed for those to be baptised at Easter, and a further set, which bear his name, on the mysteries of baptism, chrism and the Eucharist for the newly baptised. He became bishop soon after. Caught up in the Arian controversy and in a rivalry with Acacius of Caesarea, he was exiled three times, once on the charge of selling church treasures to feed the poor in a famine. In all he spent some sixteen years away from his see. He took part in the Council of Constantinople in 381, which confirmed the faith of Nicaea and his own orthodoxy, and died in Jerusalem in 386.
prayerTo: Saint Cyril, you taught the newly baptised to receive the Body of Christ as a king, with reverence and wonder. Pray for catechists and for all preparing to enter the Church this Easter. Help me to know the Creed I profess and to treasure the sacraments I receive. Amen.
penance: Pray today for those to be baptised or received into the Church this Easter in your parish, and read the Creed slowly, one article at a time.
meditation: The lectures that bear his name teach the communicant to make the left hand a throne for the right, since it is to receive a King. How do you approach Holy Communion?
